title: Apollo 7, 1968 — the crew with colds who argued with Mission Control
sources: Wikipedia: Apollo 7 — first crewed flight of the Apollo program, launched 11 October 1968, resuming crewed flights after the Apollo 1 fire killed three astronauts in a launch rehearsal on 27 January 1967; crew Walter Schirra (45, the oldest person to that point to enter space, the only astronaut to fly Mercury, Gemini and Apollo), Donn Eisele, Walter Cunningham; Saturn IB; first hot meal prepared on an American spacecraft; Schirra brought instant coffee over the opposition of NASA doctors; by the end of the first day Schirra reported a cold; the first live television broadcast from an American spacecraft on 14 October, opening with a card 'From the Lovely Apollo Room high atop everything'; tension with ground controllers; Eisele: 'somebody down there screwed up royally'; Schirra refused advice to wear helmets for reentry, fearing their eardrums might burst with their colds — 'I'm on board, I'm commanding'; no helmets were worn; splashdown 22 October; General Sam Phillips: '101 percent of our objectives'; Apollo 8 flew to the Moon two months later; none of the crew flew in space again; they were the only Apollo crew not given the Distinguished Service Medal after their mission — awarded in October 2008, when only Cunningham was alive; Schirra turned his cold into an Actifed advertising contract
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1984 Kathryn D. Sullivan becomes the first American woman to walk in space; 1986 Reagan and Gorbachev meet at the Reykjavík Summit

post.facebook:
On this day in 1968, Apollo 7 launched: the first Apollo flight with a crew, after the fire that killed the three astronauts of Apollo 1.

Commander Wally Schirra brought instant coffee, against his doctors' advice. By the end of the first day he had a cold. The crew still made the first live TV broadcast from an American spacecraft, opening with a card: "From the Lovely Apollo Room high atop everything."

But tempers ran short. "Somebody down there screwed up royally," Donn Eisele told the ground. For re-entry, Houston wanted helmets on; Schirra, afraid their blocked ears might burst, refused: "I'm on board, I'm commanding." They came home without helmets, and the mission met "101 percent" of its objectives. Two months later, Apollo 8 flew around the Moon.

None of the three ever flew in space again. They were the only Apollo crew not given NASA's Distinguished Service Medal after their mission — it came in 2008, when only Walter Cunningham was still alive.

Also on 11 October: Kathryn Sullivan became the first American woman to walk in space (1984).

youtube.description:
Apollo 7 launched on 11 October 1968 — the first crewed Apollo flight, after the Apollo 1 fire. Commander Wally Schirra brought instant coffee against his doctors' advice, caught a cold on day one, and the crew's tempers ran short. For re-entry he refused to wear his helmet: "I'm on board, I'm commanding." The mission met 101 percent of its goals and opened the way to the Moon — but none of the three ever flew in space again. Their medals came 40 years later.

Also on 11 October: Kathryn Sullivan, the first American woman to walk in space (1984).
